study type: retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional survey
cohort: The study included 47 women who underwent transvaginal uterine-preserving pelvic organ prolapse surgery (either uterosacral ligament hysteropexy or sacrospinous ligament hysteropexy) between May 2016 and December 2017.
finding: The study found no significant differences in pelvic organ prolapse recurrence or other pelvic floor outcomes between uterosacral ligament hysteropexy and sacrospinous ligament hysteropexy at approximately 2 years, with both approaches associated with high patient satisfaction.
